Run a version and check the project

Source: R/verify.R
verify.Rd

verify() runs <version>_run.R in a new R session, and then checks the project with the rules of check_project(). It prints a short verdict: the exit status of the run, each failed assertion of check.csv, and each FAIL and WARN finding.

Usage

verify(version, home = ".")

Arguments

version

The version, "v" and two digits, for example "v01".

home

The project folder. The run script runs with it as the working directory, as Rscript v01_run.R does when you start it there.

Value

Invisibly, a list with three elements. status is the exit status of the run. assertions is a data.frame of the failed assertions, with the columns file, assertion, expected and observed. findings holds the findings, as check_project() returns them.

Details

The new R session is that of callr::rscript(), with the library paths of this session. The output of the run shows as it comes.

verify() reads only the check.csv files of this run. These are the files <version>_results/<scenario>/check.csv that changed at or after the start of the run. Before the run starts, verify() waits for the next whole second, up to 1 second, and that second is the start. So a check.csv of an earlier run is older than the start, also on a file system that keeps the time of a change in whole seconds. The failed assertions are the rows of these files with a value of pass that is not TRUE.

The verdict is FAIL when one of these is true:

  • the run ends with a status other than 0.

  • the run wrote no check.csv. Then it checked no fake scenario, for example because it stopped before save_results().

  • a check.csv of the run has a failed assertion. This holds at each level of the rule scenario_checks in pbn.yml, also off.

  • a rule of check_project() fails.

Else the verdict is PASS. The last line names each reason of a FAIL. In a non-interactive R session, verify() quits R with status 1 after a verdict FAIL, as check_project() does.

See also

Other checks: check_project(), freeze_version()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
pbn::verify("v01")
}
